prerequisites: Having studied Physics in 2nd year of high school (bachillerato)
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, basic geometry, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems within their area of study, primarily enhancing the reasoning aspect over pure memorization.
Ability to plan and organize personal work.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability for effective oral and written communication.
Possess necessary learning skills to undertake further studies or improve their training with a certain degree of autonomy.
Be motivated by quality and continuous improvement and act with rigor in professional development.
Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of fields and waves and their application to solving engineering problems.
Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.
Understand the concept of a wave and know its mathematical characterization as well as basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and put into practice problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the subject.
Acquire the skills related to laboratory work and to the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Carga eléctrica. Ley de Coulomb. Campo y potencial electrostático creados por cargas puntuales. Obtención de los mismos creados por distribuciones de carga sin simetría total. Obtención del campo eléctrico creado por distribuciones de carga con simetría total: Teorema de Gauss. Obtención del potencial electrostático creado por estas últimas distribuciones de carga. Conductores. Dieléctricos: Condensadores.
Intensidad y densidad de corriente eléctrica. Ley de Ohm. Resistencia: asociaciones de las mismas. Efecto Joule. Generadores: Fuerza electromotriz. Circuitos de corriente continua.
Magnetostática: acciones de campos magnéticos sobre corrientes.
Campo magnético. Inducción magnética. Ley de Lorentz. Efecto Hall. Fuerza magnética sobre una corriente eléctrica. Momento del campo magnético sobre una espira.
Magnetostática: campos magnéticos creados por corrientes.
Ley de Biot-Savart: aplicación a conductores con simetrías de interés. Fuerza entre corrientes: redefinición de amperio. Teorema de Ampère.
Campos electromagnéticos variables con el tiempo.
Inducción electromagnética: Ley de Faraday-Henry. Autoinducción e inducción mutua.
Concepto de onda. Ecuación de ondas. Clasificación de ondas. Ondas armónicas. Ondas sonoras. Ondas estacionarias en cuerdas vibrantes. Efecto Doppler.
PL.1. Medidas eléctricas con múltimetros. Comprobación experimental de la ley de Ohm.
PL.2. Comprobación experimental del transitorio de carga de un condensador.
PL.3. Comprobación experimental de los campos magnéticos creados por: conductores rectilíneos infinitos y finitos y espiras circulares.
PL.4. Comprobación experimental de parámetros físicos asociados con ondas estacionarias generadas en cuerdas vibrantes.
teaching_methods: Expository classes (exposition and explanation of theoretical content, exemplification, problem-solving, large group evaluation activities)
Classroom practices / Seminars (problem-solving, group work activities, exposition and defense of problems/works/projects, small group evaluation activities)
Laboratory practices (handling of laboratory measurement equipment, use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing, analysis of results, very small group evaluation activities)
Individual and group study of theoretical-practical content
Problem-solving and report elaboration on proposed works
Use of virtual platforms for teaching activities

assessment_methods.method: Objective written theoretical and/or practical tests (individual)
Global Final Exam of the subject
Evaluation of laboratory practices or final laboratory practice exam
Attendance control, behavior, attitude and professor's notes on active student participation in individual and collective activities during the learning process

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum of 75% participation in all in-person activities is required. The final grade is calculated as Note Final = CT + CEF*(8,5-CT)/8,5 + CL, where CT (Theory Qualification) is over 4 points, CL (Laboratory Qualification) is over 1.5 points, and CEF (Final Exam Qualification) is over 8.5 points. To pass, a minimum final grade of 5 points (50%) is needed, with a minimum of 3 points in the final exam (CEF) and 0.5 points in laboratory practices (CL). If these minimums are not met, the maximum grade will be 4 points. For global assessment, the final grade is Note Final = CEF + CL, requiring a minimum of 5 points (50%) and 0.5 points in laboratory practices. In extraordinary calls, for continuous assessment students, CT and CL are maintained, and the student must take the final theory exam (CEF) and, if necessary, the laboratory practice exam. For global assessment students, they must take and pass both the theory (CEF) and laboratory (CL) exams.
